briefdescription.para: Handle all pending events.

detaileddescription.para: This function is not blocking: if there's no pending event then it will return without calling any of the handlers.

This function can take a variadic list of event handlers that each take a concrete event type as a single parameter. The event handlers can be any kind of callable object that has an operator() defined for a specific event type. Additionally a generic callable can also be provided that will be invoked for every event type. If both types of callables are provided, the callables taking concrete event types will be preferred over the generic callable by overload resolution. Generic callables can be used to customize handler dispatching based on the deduced type of the event and other information available at compile time.

parameterdescription.para: A variadic list of callables that take a specific event as their only parameter

briefdescription.para: Enable or disable automatic key-repeat.

detaileddescription.para: If key repeat is enabled, you will receive repeated KeyPressed events while keeping a key pressed. If it is disabled, you will only get a single event when the key is pressed.

briefdescription.para: Change the joystick threshold.

detaileddescription.para: The joystick threshold is the value below which no JoystickMoved event will be generated.

briefdescription.para: Request the current window to be made the active foreground window.

detaileddescription.para: At any given time, only one window may have the input focus to receive input events such as keystrokes or mouse events. If a window requests focus, it only hints to the operating system, that it would like to be focused. The operating system is free to deny the request. This is not to be confused with setActive().

detaileddescription.para: The type of the returned handle is sf::WindowHandle, which is a type alias to the handle type defined by the OS. briefdescription.para: Processes an event before it is sent to the user.

detaileddescription.para: This function is called every time an event is received from the internal window (through pollEvent or waitEvent). It filters out unwanted events, and performs whatever internal stuff the window needs before the event is returned to the user.

Window that serves as a base for other windows.

detaileddescription.para: sf::WindowBase serves as the base class for all Windows.
A sf::WindowBase can create its own new window, or be embedded into an already existing control using the create(handle) function.

The sf::WindowBase class provides a simple interface for manipulating the window: move, resize, show/hide, control mouse cursor, etc. It also provides event handling through its pollEvent() and waitEvent() functions.
